'''Amir Leshem''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: אמיר לשם; born: 1966) is an [[Israelites|Israeli]] [[mathematician]] and [[Research|researcher]]. He is a full [[professor]] at the Alexander Kofkin Faculty of Engineering at [[Bar-Ilan University|Bar‑Ilan University]], where he heads the Signal Processing, Information Networks & Radio Astronomy (SPIRAL) Lab.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Amir Leshem |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37284802600 |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org}}</ref>

His research spans [[signal processing]], [[Multi-agent learning|multi‑agent learning]], [[game theory]], [[wireless communications]], and [[radio astronomy]] imaging. Leshem is an [[IEEE]] [[Fellow]] "for contributions to multi-channel and multi-agent signal processing".<ref>{{Cite web |title=46 SPS Members Elevated to Fellow {{!}} IEEE Signal Processing Society |url=https://signalprocessingsociety.org/newsletter/2022/01/46-sps-members-elevated-fellow |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=signalprocessingsociety.org}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Amir Leshem was born in [[Petah Tikva]]. He graduated the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] [[Talpiot program]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.Sc.]] in [[mathematics]] and [[physics]], at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]. He earned his [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics at the Hebrew University under the supervision of [[Menachem Magidor]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2020-12-21 |title=Tutorials |url=https://icc2021.ieee-icc.org/tutorials.html#:~:text=Leshem |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240423020349/https://icc2021.ieee-icc.org/tutorials.html#:~:text=Leshem |archive-date=2024-04-23 |access-date=2025-11-04 |work=IEEE International Conference on Communications |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Amir Leshem - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=30224 |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Leshem was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Delft University of Technology]] from 1998 to 2000. He joined Bar‑Ilan University in 2002 as a senior lecturer and was the first tenured faculty member of the Alexander Kofkin Faculty of Engineering. He was promoted to full professor in 2010 and served as head of the Signal Processing track and Communication track.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=OUR TEAM {{!}} Spiral |url=https://www.eng.biu.ac.il/spiral/people/ |access-date=2025-11-04 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Leshem was an [[associate editor]] of IEEE Trans. on Signal Processing and associate editor of , IEEE Transactions on Signal and Information processing over Networks.<ref name=":0" />

He was also a [[visiting scholar]] at [[Stanford University]], [[Boston University]] and Delft University of Technology.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=CISE Resident Scholars Program {{!}} Center for Information & Systems Engineering |url=https://www.bu.edu/cise/programs/faculty-programs/cise-residents-scholars-program/ |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=www.bu.edu}}</ref>

Leshem has supervised more than 30 graduate students and authored over 200 scientific publications and 4 [[Patent|patents]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curriculum Vitae and list of publications AMIR LESHEM |url=https://www.eng.biu.ac.il/leshema/files/2019/08/%D7%9E%D7%A2%D7%95%D7%93%D7%9B%D7%9F-8.2019.pdf |website=Bar-Ilan University}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Amir Leshem |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=fkF_NmMAAAAJ |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Inventor: Amir Leshem |url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Amir+Leshem |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=patents.google.com}}</ref>

In 2024 Leshem, together with Vered Tohar, created the first Hebrew poetry book authored by an artificial intelligence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=שירת הבינה |url=https://www.kan.org.il/content/kan/podcasts/p-8266/986487/ |access-date=2026-01-06 |website=www.kan.org.il |language=he}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=אפרון (שם מומצא) |first=נעמי |title=מחברת השירים של המוזה הרהוטה |last2=טוהר |first2=ורד |last3=לשם |first3=אמיר |publisher=יצירה עברית |year=2025 |language=he |doi=10.71766/xxsk-wh36}}</ref>

== Research ==
His research work focuses on wireless networks, learning over networks, applications of game theory to networks, multi-channel communication, dynamic and adaptive [[Spectrum Management and Telecommunications|spectrum management]], [[statistical signal processing]], multi-agent learning and radio-astronomical imaging. He is also interested in [[set theory]], [[logic]] and the [[foundations of mathematics]] and [[Data processing|information processing]] in [[Social networking service|social networks]].<ref name=":1" />

== Honors and awards ==
Leshem is an IEEE fellow "for contributions to multi-channel and multi-agent signal processing" and fellow of the Asia‑Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association. He also received the Bar‑Ilan University Rector’s Award for Scientific Innovation.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Asia-Pacific Artificial Intelligence Association |url=https://aaia-ai.org/fellows?page=4 |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=aaia-ai.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=amqJ3doesU0 |title=פרופ' אמיר לשם - פרס הרקטור לחדשנות מדעית תשע"ט |date=2019-07-09 |last=Bar-Ilan University - אוניברסיטת בר-אילן |access-date=2025-11-05 |via=YouTube}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Leshem is also a landscape [[photographer]]. He participated in the group exhibition ''The Magic of Nature'' at the Tel‑Hai Photography Museum and won the excellence prize in the photography category at the 9th Geoje International Art Festival in [[South Korea]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024 |title=דו-קיום גם בזמן מלחמה: שיתוף פעולה אומנותי בינלאומי בין עשרות מדינות בעולם |url=https://www.maariv.co.il/culture/theater-art/article-1081686 |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=www.maariv.co.il |language=he}}</ref>

* G. Yujie, A. Leshem. (2012) "Robust Adaptive Beamforming Based on Interference Covariance MatrixReconstruction and Steering Vector Estimation".  IEEE Trans. on Signal Processing, vol.60, no.7, pp.3881-3885, July 2012. DOI: 10.1109/TSP.2012.2194289.
* I. Bistritz & A. Leshem. Distributed Multi-Player Bandits - a Game of Thrones Approach. 2018 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2018), Dec. 2018, Montreal, Canada.
